item.title: Xinhua Headlines: How China mounts multi-pronged rescue after deadly mudslide
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
* China has sent more than 2,300 emergency personnel into a multipronged rescue mission at the mudslide-devastated port. * Rescuers have described the mission as highly challenging due to cut-off road access, adverse weather and high risks of secondary disasters. * Before a key road was basically restored on Wednesday morning, rescuers had to trek miles through tough terrain carrying heavy loads to reach the site. * While urgently carrying out rescue and relief efforts at home, China also immediately reached out to Nepal to support its emergency response and disaster relief. GYIRONG, Xizang, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Road access to the mudslide-hit Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region was basically restored on Wednesday morning, facilitating the entry of more rescuers and machinery to assist in a large-scale search for the hundreds of people still missing. The road became accessible again after days of round-the-clock repair work, allowing more rescue teams, relief supplies and large equipment into the disaster zone. A fast-moving chain mudslide, triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal, struck Gyirong Port on the China-Nepal border in Xizang on Aug. 26. Twenty-one people have been confirmed dead and 541 others remain missing, according to the regional government's latest update. China has sent more than 2,300 emergency personnel into a multipronged rescue mission at the devastated port. Rescuers have described the mission as highly challenging due to cut-off road access, adverse weather and high risks of secondary disasters. TRUDGING TO BORDER GATE The mudslide destroyed a section of G216, a key national highway leading into the port, while strong winds and turbulence made it difficult for helicopters to airdrop rescuers at the badly-hit border gate. To reach the site, rescuers had to trek through thick mud for several kilometers carrying heavy loads. On the morning of Aug. 26 immediately after the disaster, firefighters in the town of Gyirong were mobilized to head for the port area more than 20 kilometers away. Their vehicle came to a halt about six kilometers from the destination. "The road was damaged and blocked," said firefighter Cering Ngoezhub, who saw excavators, car wrecks, clothing fragments and construction boards floating in the river nearby. Another rescuer, Nyima Gyaincain, waded through the muddy water carrying equipment weighing over 20 kilograms. "The mud was up to my calves," he said. "Every time I pulled my legs out, it was like a tug-of-war with the mud. After walking just a few dozen meters, my legs were already aching and trembling." The first team of 141 rescuers, as well as a high-altitude helicopter, arrived at the port on Thursday morning. On Friday, two teams, comprising 21 people and a search dog, became the first professional rescue teams to reach the core rescue zone at the border gate. Huo Jianxin, who led one of the teams, said they trudged between a cliff face prone to sudden landslides and a steep valley. "Our guide told us that they hadn't trekked through this primeval jungle for 20 years," Huo recalled. They relied on ropes to pass steep cliffs. "We carried loads weighing over 10 kilograms. On the descent, we had to press ourselves tightly against the mountainside and slowly slide down, relying on the friction between our bodies and the slope surface." Guo Xiqing, another team member, said that while the straight-line distance was only six kilometers, they traversed more than 20 kilometers of mountains, descending over 500 meters on ropes in total. "I have never encountered a disaster situation so complex and ever-changing," said the veteran rescuer, who has been engaged in rescue work for nearly 20 years. Search and rescue operations began immediately upon their arrival at the border gate, with the objective of locating survivors and remains of the deceased from the surface and within the crevices of the debris, paving the way for subsequent deep dredging and recovery efforts. A total of 27 buildings were flattened within the port's core area, which spanned approximately 0.7 square kilometers. A three-dimensional search and rescue tactic was adopted, combining ground operations, waterway searches, and aerial reconnaissance and delivery, supported by Beidou navigation terminals, drones, life detectors, and search and rescue dogs. "Is anybody here?" the team members shouted every few meters, their voices reverberating over the ruins. "Due to the interference from mud and standing water caused by the mudslide, life detectors couldn't function properly," said Guo. "Rescuers sometimes had to rely on visual searches, lining up in a row and conducting thorough manual inspections. After a while, the upstream area was on the verge of collapsing again, and we had no choice but to move to higher ground." RESTORING VITAL ARTERY Repair of the G216 national highway was another priority, with road access essential for vehicles and large equipment to enter the core rescue area. Operations had been hampered by extremely limited working space, difficulties in transporting large rocks needed to rebuild the roadbed, strong river currents that could wash away road-filling materials, and risks from rain, rockfalls and landslides. "Conditions vary from one section of the road to another," said Zhou Gang from China Anneng, a state-owned engineering and rescue enterprise, which deployed personnel and equipment to repair the road. Some parts of the roadbed were severely damaged, buried in mud or submerged in water. The work zone lay in a narrow mountain gorge, with steep mountainsides on one side and the fast-flowing river on the other. The confined space made it difficult for multiple pieces of heavy machinery to operate simultaneously or maneuver around one another, Zhou added. In sections where the roadbed had been washed away, excavators also risked becoming bogged down in the mud. The river was flowing at 6 to 7 meters per second and was about 1.5 meters at its deepest point, with strong currents capable of washing away ordinary rocks used to rebuild the roadbed. Supplying heavier rocks posed another challenge: with the road steep, narrow and running alongside cliffs, transporting the material from 40 kilometers away took about three hours. Crews adapted their methods to conditions. Along narrow sections, multiple excavators worked in relay, lining up one behind another to dig and pass debris from one machine to the next. They also used the river itself to separate usable material from the debris. Excavators agitated mixtures of mud, sand and rocks in the water, allowing the current to wash away fine mud while leaving behind sand and rocks that could be used to rebuild the roadbed -- a method rarely used in conventional road repairs. In sections with the strongest currents, excavators pushed into the water to open the way, while crews built diversion structures and placed rock-filled steel cages to stabilize the roadbed, advancing section by section. To guard against potential hazards as the work progressed, China Anneng used AI-enabled laser video monitoring systems to monitor surrounding mountainsides around the clock. CONTINUING RELIEF EFFORTS China has employed multiple technologies, including satellite remote sensing, radar, drones and 3D laser scanners, to monitor secondary geological hazards such as landslides and barrier lakes. The barrier lake above Gyirong Port was fully drained, with water now flowing through the river channel, according to an assessment by a team of experts on Tuesday. But the danger has not passed. Conditions in the downstream river channel still need to be closely monitored, said Ding Haitao, a senior engineer at the Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment under the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Frontline support has also been intensified. The People's Liberation Army Xizang Military Command has delivered food, medicine and rescue equipment to the core disaster area by helicopter, while city and county-level support teams in Xigaze have assisted more than 4,300 disaster-affected residents and rescue workers. An epidemic prevention team also rushed to the frontline, carrying out environmental disinfection, food and water quality testing, emergency vaccinations, and routine medical rounds for injuries and illnesses, while medical personnel at resettlement sites provide regular psychological counseling for rescuers and the disaster-affected residents. As of 5 p.m. Tuesday, telecom operators in Xizang had restored one base station and added 12 emergency base stations in disaster-hit areas, ensuring uninterrupted communications for emergency command, rescue operations and supply coordination. While urgently carrying out rescue and relief efforts at home, China also immediately reached out to Nepal to support its emergency response and disaster relief, said Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun at a news briefing on Monday. China has provided Nepal with emergency cash assistance, humanitarian aid and expert support. On Sunday, the first batch of 50 tonnes of relief supplies arrived in Kathmandu, while rescue teams composed of Chinese tunnel rescue experts rushed to disaster-stricken areas. A second round of assistance followed on Tuesday, including water purification and lighting equipment, genetic testing devices and drones, along with a team of Chinese DNA experts to support victim identification efforts. "China will stand firmly together with Nepal and jointly overcome the difficulties as part of our efforts to carry forward the traditional friendship as neighboring countries," Guo stated at a daily news briefing on Tuesday. He told another regular press briefing that China is preparing a third batch of emergency relief supplies, including Bailey bridges, epidemic prevention materials and emergency communications equipment. China is ready to send a second group of DNA identification experts based on Nepal's needs, Guo added. (Video reporters: Lodro Gyatso, Purbu Tsering, Huang Zhiqi, Sonam Dekyi, Jiang Fan, Jigme Dorje, Xue Chen, Tao Ye and Dong Bohan; Video editors: Shang Yang, Zhu Cong, Li Qin, Yu Jiaming and Zhu Jianhui) ■

item.title: China's annual IP conference to highlight high-quality development
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
BEIJING, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- The 15th China Intellectual Property Annual Conference (CIPAC) will be held from Sept. 8 to 9 in Beijing, highlighting the high-quality development of the IP sector during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), the country's top intellectual property regulator said on Wednesday. This year's conference will bring together representatives from government, industry, academia, and research and application sectors at home and abroad to jointly explore new pathways for intellectual property to serve the country's comprehensive innovation, high-quality development, and high-standard opening-up, according to the China National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA). It will focus on industrial hotspots and cutting-edge issues via one main forum, 13 parallel sessions and over 20 events. The conference will feature services for international patents, trademarks, and products, as well as Chinese and foreign geographical indication products. A total of 135 intellectual property service providers will offer end-to-end services for innovation entities. Since its inauguration in 2010, the annual CIPAC has become a high-end platform for showcasing China's development in the intellectual property sector, facilitating exchanges on cutting-edge industry topics, and promoting related services. The number of high-value invention patents held on the Chinese mainland had reached 2.29 million by the end of last year, growing at a faster pace than that of overall invention patents, according to data from the CNIPA. The number of valid invention patents held on the Chinese mainland had reached 5.32 million by the end of 2025. The year-on-year growth rate of high-value invention patents was 2.2 percentage points higher than that of the country's total invention patents last year. ■

item.title: Xi calls for deepening China-Egypt cooperation, raises Mideast proposal
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
Xi said the China-Egypt comprehensive strategic partnership has achieved leapfrog development in recent years under the guidance of the two heads of state. In the talks, Xi raised a four-point proposal on building a new security architecture in the Middle East, saying that China supports countries in the region in developing good-neighborly and friendly relations. CAIRO, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called on China and Egypt to support each other, deepen cooperation, and continue advancing the building of a China-Egypt community with a shared future amid a turbulent international and regional landscape. Xi made the remarks during his talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, while emphasizing China's support for regional countries in building a new security architecture in the Middle East via upholding a vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security. ENHANCING BILATERAL EXCHANGES, COOPERATION Noting that Egypt was the first Arab and African nation to establish diplomatic ties with the People's Republic of China in 1956, Xi said that the older-generation leaders of the two countries led their peoples in fighting side by side for national independence and against imperialism and colonialism, forging an unbreakable bond of friendship. Over the past seven decades, China-Egypt relations have weathered challenges and developed distinctive features of equality and mutual trust, friendship and mutual learning, solidarity and mutual support, as well as win-win cooperation, he said. Xi said the China-Egypt comprehensive strategic partnership has achieved leapfrog development in recent years under the guidance of the two heads of state. The two sides share similar views and have closely aligned strategies in pursuing development and revitalization, improving people's well-being, and upholding international fairness and justice, he added. Xi emphasized that China and Egypt should firmly support each other, maintain the momentum of high-level exchanges, enhance exchanges and cooperation in all fields and at all levels, and strengthen exchanges and mutual learning on governance experience. Xi said the two sides should promote mutually beneficial cooperation, better align their development strategies, tap the potential for cooperation in traditional fields such as infrastructure development, power, agriculture and communications technology, and foster new highlights of cooperation in green energy, electric vehicles, aerospace, the digital economy and modern agricultural technology. The two sides should promote people-to-people exchanges, comprehensively expand exchanges and cooperation in culture, education, science and technology, health, sports and other fields, and facilitate personnel exchanges and enhance people-to-people bonds, Xi said. The two sides should strengthen security cooperation, jointly combat transnational crime, deepen international cooperation in anti-corruption, firmly support each other's anti-terror efforts, and safeguard their common security, Xi said. The two sides should strengthen multilateral collaboration, further enhance coordination and cooperation on multilateral platforms such as the United Nations and the BRICS, jointly promote the development of the China-Arab States Cooperation Forum and the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, jointly oppose unilateralism and acts of bullying, and promote a more just and equitable global governance system, Xi said. For his part, Sisi welcomed Xi's historic state visit to Egypt on the occasion of the 70th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two countries. Sisi said that since the establishment of diplomatic relations, bilateral ties have developed in a sound and steady manner, and cooperation across various fields has yielded fruitful results. Egypt firmly adheres to the one-China principle and is committed to further advancing the Egypt-China comprehensive strategic partnership, Sisi added. Egypt is ready to work with China to deepen cooperation in trade and investment, manufacturing, infrastructure development, finance, science and technology, and new energy, strengthen military and security exchanges, and promote closer people-to-people exchanges, so as to benefit the two peoples and contribute to regional development and prosperity, Sisi said. Sisi said China, as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, plays an important and constructive role in international affairs. Egypt is ready to strengthen coordination with China at multilateral platforms, jointly address global challenges, and work together to uphold international fairness and justice, he added. The two heads of state jointly witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents on Belt and Road cooperation, artificial intelligence, economic and trade, and industrial and supply chain cooperation. The two sides also issued a joint statement on further deepening their comprehensive strategic partnership, and signed more than 20 cooperation documents covering such areas as digital economy, science and technology, education, and transportation. NEW REGIONAL SECURITY ARCHITECTURE In the talks, Xi raised a four-point proposal on building a new security architecture in the Middle East, saying that China supports countries in the region in developing good-neighborly and friendly relations. To promote common security in the region, Xi said that efforts should be made to foster the internal driving force for common security in the region. People in the Middle East should remain masters of their own affairs, and external interference should be rejected, Xi said, noting that China supports regional countries in strengthening dialogue on peace and security, exploring the building of a new security architecture for the Middle East, and taking their future into their own hands. Xi said that a comprehensive approach should be adopted to advance common security in the region and that given the multiple hotspots in the Middle East and their close interconnections, comprehensive solutions should be pursued. The Palestinian issue remains at the core of the Middle East question and should never be overlooked or marginalized, he added. The foundation for common security should be strengthened through development, Xi said, noting that lasting peace and stability in the Middle East fundamentally depend on development. China stands ready to work with Middle East countries to safeguard the security of international shipping lanes, advance development cooperation, promote the convergence of interests of regional countries, gradually enhance mutual trust, and eliminate the root causes of the conflict, he said. Xi urged that international coordination for common security in the region should be strengthened, and the UN Charter and international law should serve as the fundamental principles for handling Middle East affairs. The international community, especially external powers, should abandon double standards in the Middle East, respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of regional countries, and safeguard regional peace and stability, Xi added. He also urged support for the United Nations' effective role in Middle East affairs. Sisi said that Egypt highly appreciates China's consistent, objective, and impartial stance on the Middle East question, noting that Egypt is committed to promoting de-escalation in the region, resolving conflicts and differences through political means, and advancing regional security and development. Egypt stands ready to continue strengthening coordination with China to ease tensions in the Middle East, safeguard regional stability, and explore a regional security architecture, Sisi said. ■

item.title: China urges Japanese authorities to make clean break with militarism to win trust: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
BEIJING, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun on Wednesday urged Japanese authorities to earnestly abide by the international obligations confirmed in the Japanese Instrument of Surrender, face up to history, make a clean break with militarism, and win the trust of its Asian neighbors and the international community through concrete actions. Guo made the remarks at a regular media briefing when answering a question about China's position on the "Enemy State Clauses" in the UN Charter. On Sept. 2, 1945, the Japanese government formally signed the Instrument of Surrender and accepted all the provisions of the Potsdam Proclamation, confirming the nature of the war of aggression launched by Japanese militarism, he said. "This historical conclusion must not be tampered with, still less should the post-war international order be challenged," Guo said, adding that the "Enemy State Clauses" remain in the UN Charter to this day, and the relevant provisions, including Articles 53, 77 and 107, remain valid as well. Guo said these clauses constitute special institutional arrangements concerning the defeated countries of World War II, aim at preventing them from once again posing a threat to international peace and security, and provide important institutional safeguards for upholding the post-war international order. "Japan joined the UN on the premise that it acknowledged the crimes of militarism and accepted the UN Charter in its entirety," he added. Guo said that the Japanese authorities not only avoid addressing their historical responsibilities, but also pay homage to Class-A war criminals of World War II, distort and whitewash the crimes of aggression, accelerate remilitarization, seek to revise the pacifist Constitution, antagonize almost all of their neighboring countries, openly interfere in other countries' internal affairs, and even issue threats of force. "The 'gray rhino' of Japan's 'new militarism' is charging toward us, once again posing a threat to peace and stability in the Asia-Pacific. It is highly necessary to fully abide by the UN Charter and reaffirm the 'Enemy State Clauses,'" said Guo. ■

item.title: China cracks down on AI misuse, removes 5.6 million pieces of unlawful, rule-violating content
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
BEIJING, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Cyberspace authorities across China have removed more than 5.61 million pieces of unlawful or rule-violating content and taken action against over 49,000 accounts as part of a nationwide campaign targeting misuse of artificial intelligence tools. The campaign against irregularities in AI applications has also dealt with more than 2,400 websites and apps found in violation of the rules, according to the Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC). It is targeting the fabrication and spread of false information using AI, the production of violent or vulgar content, AI-enabled impersonation of real people, and content that infringes on the rights of minors. The latest move comes as China continues to refine its regulatory framework for generative AI, following rules that took effect in August 2023 requiring providers of generative AI services to fulfill personal information protection obligations, and content-labeling regulations, effective from September 2025, that require AI-generated text, images, audio and video to carry visible or embedded identifiers. Regional authorities have adopted differing enforcement approaches, the CAC said. In Beijing, authorities have directed platforms to upgrade content-review systems to better detect new variants of banned material, while Shanghai regulators have pushed platforms to conduct internal audits and issued public-facing materials explaining AI-related risks. Major Chinese online platforms, including Douyin, Kuaishou, Weibo, Tencent, Baidu, Bilibili, Xiaohongshu, Zhihu, Douban and Taobao, have strengthened multimodal detection systems and expanded databases used to identify manipulated faces, cloned voices and known violation samples, according to the CAC. AI chatbot and content-generation services, including ByteDance's Doubao, Tencent's Yuanbao, Alibaba's Qwen and Baidu's Ernie Bot, have tightened review of training and output content and stepped up compliance with the AI-labeling requirements, the regulator said. Smartphone app stores run by Huawei, Xiaomi, OPPO and Vivo have also introduced stricter vetting standards for app developers, including rechecking apps already listed on their platforms. The CAC published examples of accounts and applications that had been penalized, including social media accounts using AI face- and voice-swapping tools to impersonate public figures, and websites and platforms hosting AI agents whose cover images, profile descriptions or generated dialogue contained sexually explicit material or other content harmful to minors. The regulator said it would continue to monitor emerging risks tied to AI-generated content and take further steps to curb misuse of the technology, while stating a parallel goal of fostering healthy and orderly development of AI applications in China. ■

item.title: Xi congratulates King Haakon VIII of Norway on accession to throne
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
BEIJING, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday sent a congratulatory message to Haakon VIII on his accession to the throne as King of Norway. Xi said that although China and Norway are geographically distant, the two countries enjoy a long-standing friendship. Norway was among the first European countries to recognize the People's Republic of China and establish diplomatic relations with it, he said. Over the past 72 years since the establishment of diplomatic relations, with the active support and promotion of the Norwegian royal family, bilateral relations have made significant progress, and cooperation in various fields has continued to expand, bringing tangible benefits to the two peoples, Xi said. The Chinese president said he attaches great importance to the development of China-Norway relations and is ready to work with King Haakon VIII to write a new chapter in the friendly exchanges between the two countries. ■

item.title: China, Egypt welcome efforts to ease tension, promote dialogue in Middle East
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
CAIRO, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- China and Egypt welcome regional and international efforts to ease tension and promote dialogue in the Middle East, according to a joint statement issued on Wednesday. In the statement, the two sides said they welcome efforts by regional countries and the international community to promote a political understanding that takes into account the concerns of all parties and contributes to peace and stability in the Gulf and the Middle East via easing tensions and enhancing dialogue. China commends Egypt for playing a key role in promoting regional security and stability, and for its sustained efforts to advance a comprehensive political settlement of geopolitical crises in the Middle East, promote good-neighborly and friendly relations, and uphold the principles of respect for national sovereignty and non-interference in internal affairs, said the statement. Egypt commends Chinese President Xi Jinping's proposals for safeguarding and promoting peace and stability in the Middle East. During Xi's state visit to Egypt, the two countries released the joint statement on further deepening their comprehensive strategic partnership. ■
